jurisdictions.name: Nashville / Davidson County
jurisdictions.office: Metro Nashville Department of Codes & Building Safety
notes: Metro Codes publishes a list of projects that need a permit, and it marks swimming pools above or below grade as requiring a permit for one- and two-family dwellings.
The same Metro Codes list says a new fence does not need a permit but must comply with the zoning code.
The Department of Codes & Building Safety is based in the Metro Office Building at 800 2nd Avenue South, 3rd floor.

sources.title: Department of Codes & Building Safety: list of building projects which may or may not require a permit

jurisdictions.name: Memphis / Shelby County
jurisdictions.office: Memphis and Shelby County Office of Construction Enforcement
notes: The Office of Construction Enforcement serves Memphis, Arlington, Germantown, Lakeland, Millington and unincorporated Shelby County.
Its page lists permit fee schedules for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits and a link to search permit activity online.

jurisdictions.name: Knoxville / Knox County
jurisdictions.office: City of Knoxville Plans Review & Inspections
notes: The city's pool barrier guidelines call for a fence at least 48 inches high and gates that open out from the pool and are self-closing and self-latching.
Those guidelines also call for a 36-inch clear zone between the barrier and any permanent object that could be used to climb it.

jurisdictions.name: Chattanooga / Hamilton County
jurisdictions.portal_name: Hamilton County Building Permit online application
notes: Hamilton County Building Inspection enforces the 2018 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, in effect since January 1, 2022.
The county says a building permit is needed for any new structure, alteration, addition or repair.
The county exempts only prefabricated pools that are under 24 inches deep, hold no more than 5,000 gallons and sit entirely above ground.
Municipalities in the county have their own inspection offices, and Red Bank handles its own permits.
The City of Chattanooga takes residential building permit applications through an OpenGov portal run by its Land Development Office.

sources.title: Request a Residential Building Permit | Chattanooga.gov

jurisdictions.name: Franklin / Williamson County
jurisdictions.office: City of Franklin Building and Neighborhood Services
notes: In unincorporated Williamson County, the Codes Compliance Department handles swimming pool fence inspections, and electrical permits come from the State of Tennessee.

state_level.note: Tennessee law requires a pool alarm on residential swimming pools holding 36 inches or more of water, according to Rutherford County's barrier and alarm agreement form.

source.title: Swimming Pool Barrier and Alarm Agreement, Rutherford County Building Codes
